## Report Header

Filing institution: Cortex Bank and Trust
Internal case reference: FIU-2024-1701
Report filed: August 20, 2024
Suspected activity: structuring / CTR avoidance
Risk tier: medium
Subjects of this report:
  Isadora Saltonstall (individual), account 38-63800-1
Review period: February 19, 2024 through July 31, 2024
Aggregate amount of activity reviewed: $135,462.60

## Activity Overview

This report relates to activity observed in account 38-63800-1, held by Isadora Saltonstall at Cortex Bank and Trust, during a review period from February 19, 2024, through July 31, 2024. The total cash deposited into the subject account during this timeframe was $135,462.60. A review of this account was initiated following a branch referral noting the customer's inquiries regarding reporting thresholds at the teller line.

Subsequent analysis identified a pattern of transactions consistent with structuring for the purpose of evading the $10,000 Currency Transaction Report filing requirement. The activity observed was characterised by a series of cash deposits, frequently clustered in amounts between $5,937.87 and $5,688.37. The reviewing analyst noted branch rotation within a single business day on several occasions, further supporting the suspicion of structuring.

The funds deposited in this manner were subsequently moved from the account, with the largest single outbound transfer during the review period being $148,388.97. The rapid movement of funds, where cash deposits were often immediately followed by same-amount outbound transfers, suggests the account is being used to facilitate the movement of structured cash. The ultimate destination of the funds included Larkfield Ventures Group LLC, Granite Point Freight Corp., and Aperture Freight Inc. The economic purpose of these transactions remains undetermined.

## Subject Background and Relationship History

Isadora Saltonstall, the primary subject, maintains account 38-63800-1 with Cortex Bank and Trust. The relationship with the bank commenced in late 2021. The subject was onboarded primarily as a retail customer, maintaining the single personal checking account under review. At account opening, the customer's declared occupation was listed as a clerical worker for a local shipping logistics firm.

The expected activity profile established during onboarding indicated that the account would be utilized primarily for the receipt of regular payroll direct deposits and the payment of standard personal living expenses. The anticipated monthly transaction volume was estimated at a low four-figure sum, with no expectation of significant cash handling or international wire activity. Consequently, the relationship was assigned a low risk rating prior to the current review.

A review of the account activity during the period from February 19, 2024, through July 31, 2024, revealed a significant deviation from the established customer profile. The observed activity was inconsistent with the declared occupation and the expected use of a personal checking account. The volume and frequency of cash deposits, coupled with the rapid subsequent transfer of funds, were not commensurate with the anticipated regular payroll deposits and standard household expenditures recorded at onboarding.

## Key Finding

The determinative finding of this review is that the structuring activity conducted by Isadora Saltonstall was not an isolated attempt to conceal personal cash holdings, but part of a coordinated effort to fund an undisclosed corporate entity. While the initial analysis focused on the aggregate cash volume deposited during the review period, the reviewing analyst established that the sub-threshold cash deposits were systematically aggregated and subsequently moved via outbound transfers. Specifically, on July 16, 2024, a consolidation transfer of $38,212.37 was executed from account 38-63800-1, directed to an external account held by Mapleford Trading Inc., which was previously unknown to Cortex Bank and Trust. The reviewing analyst determined that the funds credited to the receiving account 11-80420-9 were entirely composed of the structured cash deposits made by the subject in the preceding weeks, indicating that the structuring was conducted with the express purpose of funding this entity while evading currency transaction reporting requirements.

## Filing Determination

Cortex Bank and Trust is filing this report because the activity described above is consistent with a customer breaking cash into sub-threshold increments to defeat currency transaction reporting and no legitimate business purpose was identified for it. The determination rests on the key finding recorded above. The relationship has been placed under enhanced monitoring, the monitoring scenarios that generated the underlying alerts have been retuned for this customer segment, and a relationship review has been scheduled. Supporting documentation is retained in internal case file FIU-2024-1701 and is available to law enforcement on request.

## Activity Overview

The review period for this investigation spans January 12, 2024 through June 25, 2024. The activity involves Dashiell Beaumont, holder of Cortex Bank and Trust account 37-30576-1. The total value of the suspected fraudulent activity is $386,340.54. The review was prompted by a branch referral following a customer inquiry regarding an unpaid vendor invoice. The activity is consistent with wire fraud, specifically an incident where funds were induced out of the customer account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay. The referral indicated that the customer believed they were remitting payment for legitimate goods or services, but the beneficiary information provided in the payment instructions was altered. The activity involves the use of the wire transfer channel. The investigation focuses on identifying the circumstances surrounding the authorization of the wire transfer and the subsequent movement of funds. The initial review of the account activity and the referral information suggests that the customer was the victim of a targeted deception.

## Subject Background and Relationship History

Dashiell Beaumont established a relationship with Cortex Bank and Trust on January 12, 2024, opening account 37-30576-1. The subject was onboarded as a sole proprietor operating in the logistics consulting sector. At the time of account opening, the relationship manager documented an expected activity profile consistent with a domestic service provider, including regular inbound payments from established clients and routine operational expenditures. The account was assigned a moderate risk rating during the onboarding process, reflecting the stated line of business and anticipated transaction volumes.

A review of the account history from account inception through June 25, 2024, revealed activity that was broadly consistent with the initial customer profile until the events precipitating this investigation. Initial transaction patterns included periodic deposits and standard business expenses. However, the anticipated domestic nature of the business was challenged by the subsequent activity, which involved a significant outward remittance that deviated from the established baseline. The reviewing analyst noted that the stated business model did not adequately explain the volume or destination of the funds transferred, necessitating a reassessment of the subject's risk profile and the nature of the transactions conducted through the account.

## Key Finding

On review of the electronic communications produced by the customer pursuant to the investigation, the reviewing analyst identified a pattern of deceptive instructions directing the diversion of vendor payments. The determinative finding of this review is that a fraudulent instruction, masquerading as a communication from an established supplier, induced the customer to initiate a wire transfer that ultimately resulted in a substantial loss. The investigation established that a portion of the diverted funds, specifically $384,608.29, was subsequently traced to an account held by Ulises Ibarra. The analyst confirmed that this specific sum was received into account 27-50806-9 on June 5, 2024. This finding corroborates the suspected typology of funds induced out of the customer account by deception and moved to a beneficiary the customer did not intend to pay.

## Filing Determination

Cortex Bank and Trust is filing this report because the activity described above is consistent with funds induced out of a customer account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay and no legitimate business purpose was identified for it. The determination rests on the key finding recorded above. The relationship has been placed under enhanced monitoring, the monitoring scenarios that generated the underlying alerts have been retuned for this customer segment, and a relationship review has been scheduled. ## Report Header

  Oriana Delacroix (individual), account 41-70226-1
Review period: January 19, 2024 through July 11, 2024
Aggregate amount of activity reviewed: $283,490.62

## Activity Overview

This report details activity conducted by Oriana Delacroix through Cortex Bank and Trust checking account 41-70226-1 between January 19, 2024 and July 11, 2024. The total value of the transactions reviewed during this period was $283,490.62. The activity under review was initially identified by the bank's automated transaction monitoring system, which generated alerts regarding potential exposure to a sanctioned jurisdiction.

A review of the transaction history indicated that the subject account received multiple incoming wire transfers and initiated outgoing payments that exhibited characteristics consistent with attempts to evade sanctions screening controls. The transactions involved counterparties including Bright Harbor Marine Services Inc., Marblehead Ventures Corp., and Falcon Crest Ventures Corp. The activity observed included instances where shipping documents appeared to be re-routed through a known transshipment hub, a common indicator of potential sanctions evasion. Furthermore, certain payment references were observed to have originator details removed. The investigation also identified a counterparty address located in a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction. An intermediate owner associated with one of the corporate entities was noted to hold exactly forty-nine percent ownership. The activity was primarily conducted via domestic wire transfers.

## Subject Background and Relationship History

Oriana Delacroix has maintained an individual checking account, number 41-70226-1, with Cortex Bank and Trust since November 2019. The customer is additionally listed as a guarantor on a home equity line of credit originated in March 2021. At the time of account opening, the customer's stated occupation was an independent logistics consultant, and the expected activity profile indicated domestic payroll deposits and standard household expenditures. The account was assigned a low risk rating during onboarding, consistent with the anticipated personal use.

A review of account activity prior to the current investigation period showed transaction patterns generally in line with the expected profile. However, beginning in late 2023, the account began receiving substantial, irregular incoming wire transfers from commercial entities. This activity diverged significantly from the anticipated personal transaction behavior. The customer's stated occupation as a logistics consultant was reviewed against the incoming commercial payments, but the volume and nature of the transfers did not align with typical consulting fee structures. The customer was not registered as a sole proprietorship or holding a designated business account with Cortex Bank and Trust. The risk rating remained low prior to this escalation.

## Key Finding

The determinative finding of this review is that Oriana Delacroix is acting as an intermediary for a party subject to sectoral sanctions, a fact established when a payment of $63,957.88 was intercepted and held in suspense account 20-47259-9. Review of the underlying trade documents for this transaction, which was routed through Bright Harbor Marine Services Inc., revealed that the ultimate beneficiary of the shipment was Ardent Capital Holdings Ltd., an entity operating in a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction. This connection was confirmed on June 17, 2024, when the relationship manager obtained the original, unredacted bill of lading, which contradicted the sanitized shipping documents previously provided by the subject. The sanitized documents had listed a transshipment hub as the final destination and omitted the originator detail, consistent with attempts to evade sanctions screening.

## Filing Determination

Cortex Bank and Trust is filing this report because the activity described above is consistent with exposure to a sanctioned party or jurisdiction that screening either missed or flagged and the business escalated incorrectly and no legitimate business purpose was identified for it. The determination rests on the key finding recorded above. The relationship has been placed under enhanced monitoring, the monitoring scenarios that generated the underlying alerts have been retuned for this customer segment, and a relationship review has been scheduled. Supporting documentation is retained in internal case file FIU-2024-1703 and is available to law enforcement on request.

## Report Header

  Bramblewood Fabrication Trading Co. (business), account 25-71605-1
Review period: January 30, 2024 through July 17, 2024
Aggregate amount of activity reviewed: $2,007,059.14

## Activity Overview

This review was initiated by Cortex Bank and Trust’s Financial Intelligence Unit following a routine quality assurance audit of onboarding files. The audit identified significant deficiencies in the customer due diligence file for Bramblewood Fabrication Trading Co., account 25-71605-1. A review of the account activity was conducted for the period from January 30, 2024, through July 17, 2024. The reviewing analyst determined that the activity conducted during the review period was not commensurate with the information documented in the customer profile and that the file lacked the necessary documentation to support the assigned medium risk rating.

During the review period, aggregate activity on the account totaled $2,007,059.14. The activity primarily consisted of incoming and outgoing wire transfers. The initial funding of the account, which occurred on February 8, 2024, involved an unverified amount of $355,937.37. The reviewing analyst noted that the account was opened with a documentary exception that was not subsequently cleared. The stated business purpose for Bramblewood Fabrication Trading Co. could not be reconciled with the observed transaction patterns, which involved counterparties such as Wheatfield Exports Partners LP, Cardinal Commodities Partners LP, and Slateford Logistics LLC. The volume and velocity of the funds transfer activity, coupled with the missing due diligence documentation, prompted a broader investigation into the account's usage.

## Subject Background and Relationship History

Account 25-71605-1, held by Bramblewood Fabrication Trading Co., was opened at Cortex Bank and Trust on January 30, 2024. The account was established as a standard commercial checking product. At the time of onboarding, the relationship manager assigned a risk tier of medium to the customer.

The customer profile recorded during the initial due diligence process indicated an expected activity profile consistent with a domestic trading operation. The anticipated monthly transaction volume was described as moderate, primarily comprising automated clearing house credits and wire transfers related to the purchase and sale of fabricated goods. The occupation or line of business field on the customer profile, however, was left blank.

Subsequent review of the account activity revealed a significant divergence from the anticipated profile. The initial funding, received on February 8, 2024, was for $355,937.37. The source of these funds could not be verified by the reviewing analyst. The declared activity, which suggested a domestic focus, bore no relation to the observed activity, which included substantial international wire transfers to entities such as Wheatfield Exports Partners LP and Cardinal Commodities Partners LP. This activity is inconsistent with the customer profile and the assigned risk tier.

## Key Finding

The determinative finding of the review period pertained to the unverified initial funding amount of $355,937.37, which the relationship manager had permitted Bramblewood Fabrication Trading Co. to receive into account 25-71605-1 prior to the completion of the beneficial ownership attestation. The reviewing analyst established that this initial funding was part of a larger, undisclosed capitalization structure. The analyst identified that a separate sum of $1,207,819.34 was routed through an unvetted intermediary, Quarrystone Textiles LLC, before being directed into a previously undisclosed holding account, 17-51708-9, controlled by the same beneficial owners. The relationship manager approved the medium risk tier assignment on June 26, 2024, despite the documentary exception remaining uncleared and the source of these funds lacking corroboration in the customer due diligence file. The declared activity in the file bore no relation to this observed capitalization method, and the aggregate activity of $2,007,059.14 conducted over the review period could not be supported by the deficient documentation.

## Filing Determination

Cortex Bank and Trust is filing this report because the activity described above is consistent with a due diligence file that cannot support the risk rating the account was given and no legitimate business purpose was identified for it. The determination rests on the key finding recorded above. The relationship has been placed under enhanced monitoring, the monitoring scenarios that generated the underlying alerts have been retuned for this customer segment, and a relationship review has been scheduled. Supporting documentation is retained in internal case file FIU-2024-1704 and is available to law enforcement on request.

## Report Header

Subjects of this report:
  Greystone Ventures Enterprises LLC (business), account 66-96376-1
Review period: November 29, 2023 through April 8, 2024
Aggregate amount of activity reviewed: $3,827,497.24

## Activity Overview

This report describes activity identified by Cortex Bank and Trust during a review period from November 29, 2023, through April 8, 2024. The subject of this review is Greystone Ventures Enterprises LLC, maintaining Cortex Bank and Trust account 66-96376-1. The review was prompted by a branch referral following a customer contact regarding a suspected compromised communication channel resulting in an unauthorized funds transfer.

The identified activity involves a single outbound wire transfer totaling $3,827,497.24, initiated from the Greystone Ventures Enterprises LLC account. The transaction pattern is consistent with wire fraud, wherein funds were induced out of the customer account by deception and moved to a beneficiary not intended by the customer. The customer reported that the transfer instructions were received via email, later determined to have originated from a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from a known vendor's domain. The instructions included urgency language that circumvented the customer's established dual-approval control, and the beneficiary name on the transfer instructions did not match the name of the invoicing vendor. Furthermore, the funds transfer was initiated minutes before the daily wire cutoff time. Following discovery of the suspected fraud, Cortex Bank and Trust contacted the receiving institution, which subsequently froze a portion of the funds.

## Subject Background and Relationship History

Greystone Ventures Enterprises LLC established a relationship with Cortex Bank and Trust on November 29, 2023, opening a single commercial checking account, numbered 66-96376-1. The onboarding documentation indicated the entity operated as a commercial real estate holding company, acquiring and managing mid-market retail properties. The declared business purpose was consistent with the initial risk rating of low. Expected activity profiled at account opening anticipated monthly inbound wire transfers from property management firms, totaling a low six-figure sum, and outbound domestic wires for property acquisitions, maintenance, and debt service. 

Initial account activity aligned with these expectations. However, a review of transaction history revealed a deviation from the expected profile beginning in early 2024. Observed activity during the review period included an outbound domestic wire transfer significantly exceeding the anticipated transaction volume and value. The transaction profile also shifted, featuring a large, anomalous outbound wire that did not align with the established pattern of property management disbursements or debt service payments. The beneficiary of this anomalous transfer was not among the previously established payees or vendors associated with the subject's declared business operations.

## Key Finding

On April 3, 2024, the reviewing analyst established that the funds induced from Greystone Ventures Enterprises LLC were not immediately dissipated by the receiving institution. A review of the receiving institution's subsequent filing indicated that a portion of the incoming wire was subjected to internal controls prior to the execution of the withdrawal requests. The analyst determined that $952,440.92 was successfully interdicted before it could be moved to an external wallet controlled by Camila Dalrymple. The receiving institution confirmed that these funds were secured in suspense account 13-83774-9 pending further instruction from law enforcement. The remaining balance of the initial wire was confirmed to have been successfully withdrawn by the beneficiary prior to the application of the freeze.

## Filing Determination

Cortex Bank and Trust is filing this report because the activity described above is consistent with funds induced out of a customer account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay and no legitimate business purpose was identified for it. The determination rests on the key finding recorded above. The relationship has been placed under enhanced monitoring, the monitoring scenarios that generated the underlying alerts have been retuned for this customer segment, and a relationship review has been scheduled. Supporting documentation is retained in internal case file FIU-2024-1707 and is available to law enforcement on request.

  Delia Vasquez (individual), account 81-28227-1
Review period: December 7, 2023 through May 9, 2024
Aggregate amount of activity reviewed: $502,466.81

## Activity Overview

This review was initiated by Cortex Bank and Trust's Financial Intelligence Unit following an escalation from the sanctions screening operations team. The escalation concerned international wire transfers originating from account 81-28227-1, held by Delia Vasquez. The activity under review spans the period from December 7, 2023, through May 9, 2024. The reviewing analyst identified potential exposure to a sanctioned jurisdiction or party. 

The aggregate value of the screened transactions during the review period was $502,466.81. The activity primarily involved outgoing international wire transfers to commercial counterparties. The escalation was prompted by a payment blocked and reported by the screening system, totaling $75,149.17. Following the block, a second payment was held pending resolution of a potential name match; this transfer was for $67,955.00. 

A review of the transaction details and accompanying documentation revealed several factors that contributed to the high risk tier assigned to this case. Counterparty information included an address located in a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction. Furthermore, the review identified shipping documents that had been re-routed through a known transshipment hub. The declared value of the shipment named in these trade documents was $75,688.40. Additional analysis identified an intermediate ownership structure where an entity held exactly forty-nine percent, and instances where payment references appeared to have been stripped of originator detail.

## Subject Background and Relationship History

Delia Vasquez established a relationship with Cortex Bank and Trust on December 7, 2023, by opening personal checking account 81-28227-1. The account was opened in branch, and Vasquez provided documentation indicating employment as a logistics coordinator for a regional import-export firm. At onboarding, the anticipated account activity profile was documented as consistent with a salaried employee, expecting bi-weekly direct deposits and routine consumer expenditures. The initial customer risk rating was assigned as low, reflecting the standard consumer profile presented.

A review of the account activity from December 7, 2023, through May 9, 2024, revealed transactional behavior inconsistent with the anticipated profile. While some payroll deposits were observed, the account experienced a high volume of incoming and outgoing wire transfers, significantly exceeding the expected activity for a salaried individual. The aggregate value of the screened transactions under review was $502,466.81. The counterparties involved in these wire transfers were primarily commercial entities, including Sandpiper Trading Corp. and Wheatfield Holdings Corp. This volume and the commercial nature of the counterparties were not aligned with the stated occupation or the expected routine consumer expenditures recorded at the time of account opening.

## Key Finding

Analysis of the transaction history associated with Delia Vasquez established that the payment processing errors initially attributed to a system outage were, in fact, deliberate diversions of funds. The reviewing analyst determined that on April 30, 2024, a series of four domestic wire transfers totaling $149,382.44 were initiated from account 81-28227-1. These transfers were routed to account 52-51693-9, an account held at a regional institution. Further investigation revealed that the beneficiary of this receiving account was Fenwick Eriksson, an individual with no documented business relationship or prior transactional history with the subject. The customer was unable to substantiate the economic purpose of these transfers when queried by the relationship manager. This activity is consistent with an attempt to obfuscate the origin and ultimate destination of the funds, suggesting potential involvement in an undisclosed business arrangement or illicit activity.

## Filing Determination

Cortex Bank and Trust is filing this report because the activity described above is consistent with exposure to a sanctioned party or jurisdiction that screening either missed or flagged and the business escalated incorrectly and no legitimate business purpose was identified for it. The determination rests on the key finding recorded above. The relationship has been placed under enhanced monitoring, the monitoring scenarios that generated the underlying alerts have been retuned for this customer segment, and a relationship review has been scheduled. Supporting documentation is retained in internal case file FIU-2024-1708 and is available to law enforcement on request.
